IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC. APPLICATION (FOR SUCCESSIVE REGULAR BAIL -  AFTER CHARGESHEET) NO.7983 of 2025  ==========================================================
 VIPULBHAI JAYSUKHBHAI VARANIYA  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR AFTABHUSEN ANSARI(5320) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  LEARNED ADVOCATE MS DIYA MITRA for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR BHARGAV PANDYA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY  Date : 07/08/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on regular bail in connection with FIR being CR. No.I- 11203007230427 of 2023 registered with Bhesan Police Station, Junagadh for the offences punishable under Sections 376AB, 376(2)
(f), 450 of the Indian Penal Code r/w Sections 4, 5(M), 6, 8 and 12 of the Preventions of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Preventions of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Heard learned Advocate appearing for the applicant.
He submitted that the applicant has been arrested in connection with the present offence on 30.09.2023 and since then he is in custody.
The investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.

1 incarceration for a period of almost two years and there has been no progress in the trial.

sentences.text: He submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties and the complainant has no objection, if the applicant is ordered to be enlarged on bail.
He has further submitted that the applicant has good reputation in the society and no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in Jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.

3. Learned APP has opposed the present application contending that the offence alleged against the present applicant is heinous in nature, and therefore, no leniency should be shown to the present applicant.
He further submitted that the trial of the offence is in progress.
Learned APP has therefore submitted that looking to the nature of offence, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.

4. Learned Advocate appearing for the complainant has submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties and the complainant has no objection if the applicant is ordered to be enlarged on bail.
She, therefore, submitted to pass an appropriate order.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7983/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 5.
Heard learned Advocates for the parties.

At the outset, it is required to be noted that the applicant had earlier preferred Criminal Misc. Application No.25535 of 2024 which was allowed to be withdrawn by this Court vide Order dated 12.02.2025 since this Court was not inclined to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant.
Learned Advocate appearing for the applicant is not in a position to show any change in circumstances after withdrawal of the earlier application filed by the applicant.
On the contrary, as pointed out by the learned APP, the trial of the offence is in progress and as many as Seven witnesses have already been examined.

Therefore, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of X versus State of Rajasthan and another, it would not be proper for this Court to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant at this stage.

entities.text: X versus State of Rajasthan and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. So far as the aspect of merits is concerned, from the record, it appears that the age of the prosecutrix was merely 8 years and 5 months at the relevant time whereas the applicant was aged 23 years.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 of Criminal Procedure Code wherein she has categorically stated that she was subjected to sexual assault by the present applicant.

7. It was contended by the learned Advocate appearing for the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7983/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined applicant as well as learned Advocate appearing for the complainant that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties.
The offence alleged against the applicant is serious in nature and is also not compoundable in nature.
However, the fact remains that despite being in custody, the applicant herein has successfully influenced the first informant and a settlement has been arrived at between the parties.
Having regard to these aspects, no case is made out.
Hence, the present application is dismissed.
